findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and crashes on use
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but implements none of its abstract methods (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the new build_occurrence_and_event_data). Instantiating it raises TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler. It is still assigned as MetricAlertFire.detector_handler, and Detector.detector_handler calls that class with no try/except. Any detector whose type slug is metric_alert_fire will therefore throw while process_detectors resolves the handler and abort the rest of the batch. The previous handler was a concrete DetectorHandler whose evaluate() returned an empty list, so this is a regression. The TODO above the class still says it will become a stateful detector later, which no longer matches the base class.

findings.title: test_dedupe expects an occurrence for the wrong group key
findings.body: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds the expected occurrence with build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH), then calls evaluate_group_key_value with group_key "group_key" and value 10. The helper sets IssueOccurrence.fingerprint from handler.build_fingerprint(group_key), so the expected fingerprint is "{detector_id}:val1" while the code under test builds "{detector_id}:group_key". DetectorEvaluationResult and IssueOccurrence compare by value, so the equality assertion fails and the later dedupe-skip assertion is never reached. The expected value 6 also does not match the evaluated value 10; that second mismatch is currently hidden only because the helper ignores value.

findings.title: Occurrence fingerprint is not tied to the resolve fingerprint
findings.body: A non-OK transition now stores whatever IssueOccurrence build_occurrence_and_event_data returns, including its fingerprint, and process_detectors publishes that occurrence. The OK transition in the same method always emits StatusChangeMessage(fingerprint=self.build_fingerprint(group_key), new_status=RESOLVED). The hook is not passed that fingerprint, the base class does not overwrite occurrence.fingerprint afterward, and the new abstract method does not require subclasses to call build_fingerprint. If those fingerprints differ, the later resolve cannot match the issue this detector opened, while detector state is still marked inactive. Tests do not lock the invariant: the mock happens to call build_fingerprint, and test_above_below_threshold hardcodes the resolve fingerprint instead of asserting it equals the firing occurrence's fingerprint.

findings.title: Occurrence tests never check the measured value
findings.body: build_mock_occurrence_and_event accepts value but never puts it on the IssueOccurrence or event_data, so result equality cannot tell whether build_occurrence_and_event_data received the measured value. Call sites also pass the wrong number and still pass: test_state_results_multi_group builds the group_2 expectation with 6 while the packet value is 10; TestEvaluate.test_results_on_change evaluates 100 but expects an occurrence built with 6; TestEvaluate.test_dedupe evaluates 8 but expects 6. A regression that forwarded the dedupe value, the threshold, or another group's value would not be caught.

findings.title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate's docstring still says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult. The method now returns a dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey, and process_detectors iterates .values() on that dict. A caller that follows the docstring and iterates the return value will get group keys rather than evaluation results.
